_comment: Controlled vocabularies for the claims and units tables. scripts/validate.py enforces these. To add a value, edit this file and schema/README.md in the same pull request.

theater.description: Theater of the claim row: the front or rear area where the unit was on the claim date (a row may differ from the unit's primary theater in data/units.csv; see the Theater section of schema/README.md). The claim's operation must carry the same theater.

values.western_europe: Northwest Europe and France: the 1940 campaign in the West, the 1940-1944 occupation of France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Luxembourg and the Channel Islands, staging in Great Britain, and the campaign from the Normandy landings to the end of the war in the West (including Germany, Austria and Czechoslovakia as the Western Allies advanced), plus southern France from the Dragoon landings (15 August 1944) on, because the project's Western Front scope includes the Riviera-to-Rhine campaign.
values.mediterranean: Italy, Sicily, Sardinia, Corsica and the Mediterranean Sea (southern France only before the Dragoon landing, for example staging in Italy or Corsica; from 15 August 1944 southern France is western_europe).
values.north_africa: Libya, Egypt, Tunisia, Algeria and Morocco campaigns (1940-1943).
values.eastern_front: Germany/Axis versus the USSR (Soviet Union, Poland, Baltic, Romania, Hungary, Slovakia, Finland), including German territory as the Red Army reached it (East Prussia, Silesia, Pomerania, the Oder front, Berlin).
values.balkans: Yugoslavia, Albania, Greece, Bulgaria and the Aegean islands (German occupation, anti-partisan operations and the 1941 and 1944-1945 campaigns).
values.scandinavia: Norway and Denmark (the 1940 invasion and the occupation to May 1945). Finland is eastern_front.
values.home_germany: Germany as then constituted (the 1937 Reich plus annexed Austria, the Sudetenland, the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia and the annexed Polish areas) as a rear or home area: forming, training, refitting and the replacement army (BdE), at places that were not then in a combat zone. Rows in Germany in the path of the Western Allies are western_europe; rows in the path of the Red Army are eastern_front.
values.pacific: Pacific Ocean areas and Southwest Pacific, including Japan, the Philippines and the Dutch East Indies.
values.atlantic: Atlantic Ocean, Arctic convoys and other naval or air units whose operations are mainly at sea.
values.other: Anything that does not fit above (for example East Africa or the Middle East). Explain in notes.

relationship.description: Meaning of the relationship column of data/command_relations.csv (and of the `relationship` key of the entries rebuilt from it for build/all_claims.csv). A relation may carry valid_from, valid_to and date_basis (see schema/README.md).

values.organic: A constituted component of the formation: its own regiments, battalions or battle groups, or a unit that is part of the parent's table of organisation. Do not use for a division, corps or army that is assigned to a higher headquarters (use assigned or unspecified_subordination).
values.assigned: The unit was assigned to this formation: the source says 'assigned', or names the unit as a standing member of the headquarters' order of battle for a period not described as temporary, with no attachment language. Includes army to army group and corps to army.
values.attached: The unit was attached to this formation (a temporary or task-organised subordination) on the row's date; use only where the source says attached or shows a temporary tasking.
values.unspecified_subordination: The source shows the unit subordinate to this formation on the date but does not distinguish assigned from attached (for example the CMH ETO-OB assignment tables, whose columns are combined). Never convert to attached or assigned without a source.
values.operational_control: This formation exercised operational (tactical) control over the unit, whether or not the unit was one of its assigned or attached components.
values.administrative_control: This formation held administrative, supply or personnel responsibility for the unit while another formation had operational control.
values.supporting: The unit was in direct support of this formation without being part of it.
values.coordinating: This formation coordinated the unit's operations with others without commanding it (for example 21st Army Group's coordination of both army groups until 1 September 1944).
values.reserve: The unit was held in this formation's (or the high command's) reserve.
values.unknown: A formation is named by the source but how it relates to the unit is not stated (for example AFHQ's retained supply, administration and civil-affairs responsibility in the area overrun on 15 September 1944, which is a theater function, not stated as control of the unit).

claim_status.description: How a row relates to competing claims. Rows with a conflict_group_id must use preferred, alternate or disputed as below; rows with no conflict are always preferred.

values.preferred: A non-conflicted claim, or the best-supported claim in a conflict group.
values.alternate: A competing claim judged less likely than the preferred one in the same conflict group.
values.disputed: One of several competing claims where no source is judged better; a group with no preferred row has all rows disputed.

values.army_group: Army group or equivalent theater command (for example 21st Army Group, Army Group B).
values.regiment/battle_group: Regiment-sized or smaller ad hoc formation such as a Kampfgruppe or an Allied combat command.
values.company: Company-sized unit (company, battery, squadron of a ground unit), recorded only when a source traces it up the chain to a parent division or higher (Scott, 4 November 2026; for example H Company, 116th Infantry, 29th Division); rank 0, no echelon letter in the id.
values.battalion: Battalion-sized or smaller formation that is only an opponent or a component of a larger unit (for example a heavy tank battalion); rank 1. Regiments and regiment-sized battle groups keep `regiment/battle_group`.
values.other: Higher or special headquarters that fit no level above (for example OB West).
values.air_force: Reserved for later: air force, air fleet or air army headquarters (not yet used).
values.air_formation: Reserved for later: air corps, air division, wing, group or squadron (not yet used).
values.naval_unit: Ship: one vessel, a commissioned combatant of destroyer-escort size or larger, or a single small craft that a source singles out and that traces to a parent (docs/air_naval_pilot.md section 6.1). Naval ladder, rank 10, no id letter.
values.naval_division: Naval division or flotilla: a destroyer division, a minesweeping, S-boat or U-boat flotilla, a landing-craft flotilla or LST group. Naval ladder, rank 11, no id letter.
values.naval_squadron: Naval squadron: a destroyer or cruiser squadron. Naval ladder, rank 12, no id letter.
values.task_group: Task unit, task group or task force (US task organisation; Royal Navy forces such as Force S and Bombarding Force D map here); the sub-label goes in the unit note. A task organisation holds command relations only and normally has no claims (record_status placeholder). Naval ladder, rank 13, no id letter.
values.fleet: Numbered fleet or naval command (Home Fleet, Seventh Fleet, Marinegruppe West). Naval ladder, rank 14, no id letter.

branch.description: Service or arm, assigned from the unit name.

values.Army: Regular army (including infantry and static divisions).
values.Luftwaffe: Luftwaffe ground formations (for example Fallschirmjaeger and Luftwaffe field divisions); also reserved for Luftwaffe flying units.
values.Marines: Marine ground formations (reserved; none served on the Western Front 1944-45).
values.Air Force: Reserved for later: air forces (RAF, USAAF, Luftwaffe flying units).

values.main_body: Where the main body of the unit was.
values.sector_center: The centre of the sector or landing zone the unit held or used.
values.front_line_point: A representative point on the unit's front line or point of contact.
values.objective: The place the unit captured, attacked or defended.
values.approach_route: A point on the unit's march or approach route.
values.base: The airfield, port or anchorage a flying or naval unit operates from (a base), as opposed to the target area it acts over (objective). Added in the air-naval schema pass, 13 November 2026.

precision_km.description: Judgment estimate, in kilometres, of the radius within which the unit (or its main body) probably was. Not a surveyed error. Banded values.

values.1: Exact named place tied to the date; division or smaller.
values.3: Village-scale point; manual override used once in the proof of concept (C0034).
values.5: Named town or village, approximate; or exact for corps and above.
values.10: Sector or beach centre (beaches are 8-10 km wide), or inferred for division or smaller.
values.25: Inferred for corps, or approximate for army and above; approach routes within one region.
values.50: Inferred for army and above, or long approach routes (for example a move from Brittany).

confidence.description: Numeric 0-1 score applied by rule from location quality and source families. Only these four levels are used.

values.0.9: Exact location and two independent source families agree (Wikipedia, CMH/HyperWar and each other domain count as separate families; several Wikipedia pages count as one).
values.0.7: Exact location with one authoritative source (for example the US Army CMH); or approximate location with two source families.
values.0.5: Exact location with one secondary source (Wikipedia, local-history page); or approximate location with one source family.
values.0.3: Position inferred or a representative point (HQ not tied to the date, unverified beach, front-line representative point), or the date itself is approximate.

rules: Caps for conflicts: the preferred row of a conflict group is at most 0.7; alternate and disputed rows are at most 0.5.
A manual override is allowed when the date itself is approximate (use 0.3) and must be explained in notes.

values.landing: Seaborne or airborne landing, including D-Day assault landings.
values.arrival: Reaching the front or the beachhead after the landing phase.
values.capture: Taking a named place or position.
values.activation: A formation becomes operational, or is activated or constituted as a headquarters or unit (for example 12th Army Group becoming operational on 1 August 1944).
values.subordinate_assignment: A source (a CMH assignment table or an order) lists the unit under a higher headquarters, or lists a headquarters' first subordinate unit, from this date; it says nothing about when command was first exercised or when a headquarters became operational. Use activation only where a source documents the operational start (taking a sector, command or mission).
values.hq_observation: A source (a command-post list, situation map or report) records the headquarters at a place on the date; it does not state that the headquarters moved on that date (use hq_move where a dated movement source exists).
values.redesignation: The same formation takes a new designation (identity continues; for example XVIII Corps becoming XVIII Airborne Corps).
values.commissioning: A ship or boat is launched, commissioned or taken into service (including transfer to another navy as a new commissioning). Added in the air-naval schema pass, 13 November 2026.
values.sortie: A flying unit's sorties or a ship's or submarine's sortie or patrol from its base (a documented mission flown or sailed, not a relocation of the unit). Added in the air-naval schema pass, 13 November 2026.
values.other: Headquarters decisions, air attack on a headquarters, units at their station.

note_label.description: Labels that may start a sentence of the claims' `notes` column in the form `Label: text` (or `Label (qualifier): text`). A sentence-initial phrase that has this shape (a capital letter and up to two more lower-case words) and is not in this list is an error. Lead-ins that name a source, a batch or an id (anything with a digit, a hyphen or a capital after the first word, and `Wikipedia`) are prose, not labels. To add a label: see schema/README.md, 'Note labels'.

values.Event date: The source for the date of the event, and how the date was fixed (108 uses at the time the set was frozen).
values.Event definition: What event this row means, needed when rows in a conflict group differ in event type or definition, for example a landing against an arrival (106).
values.Event support: How well the event itself is documented, in words (high, moderate, low) with the source; `confidence` scores the location, this sentence the event (70).
values.Location: What the point stands for and which source places it (100).
values.Location support: How well the location is documented, in words, with the source (70).
values.Location support fallback: The location support when the point is only a fallback such as a sector point (1).
values.Location caveat: A doubt about the place name or the point that the row's coordinates do not remove (3).
values.Location approximate: The point is approximate and says how (1).
values.Coordinates: How the numbers were obtained: gazetteer, centroid, measured on a map (55).
values.Coordinate check: The outcome of a coordinate or speed check against another claim (1).
values.Relationship: The source for the command relationship of the row (102).
values.Command support: How well the command event (start of command, hour, date) is documented (1).
values.Opponents: What is and is not covered by `engaged_with` (1).
values.Objective check: Why `location_represents` objective holds on the row date (8).
values.Commander: The source for the commander named in the row (1).
values.Context: Background that explains the row but does not belong to it (1).
values.Later: What later sources or rows show about the same fact (1).
values.Search: What was searched and not found, and where (1).
values.Review: A later review's correction of the row and what it changed (1).
values.Activity: The activity_status of the row: its basis and, for a change to an existing row, the old value, the new value and the reason.

strength_status.description: Qualitative strength as it appears in build/all_claims.csv (a derived value, not a claim-file column): destroyed when the claim's destroyed flag is true, else the `status` key of strength_json, else unknown. Default unknown; a status is set only when a source states strength or losses.

values.full: A source describes the unit as at full strength.
values.reduced: Source states significant losses or reduced combat power.
values.heavily_depleted: Source states the unit was a small fraction of its strength.
values.destroyed: Unit destroyed or ceased to exist as a fighting formation.

strength_json_basis.description: Meaning of the basis field inside strength_json.

values.reported_actual: A unit report or operational count relayed by the source (for example working-order tank returns).
values.authorized_organization: Establishment or table-of-organisation strength, not an actual count.
values.estimate: Rounded, approximate or retrospective figure, or a landing tally.
values.refit: A dated change of a ship's capabilities from its class figures (a refit); carried in strength_json under capabilities (docs/air_naval_pilot.md section 6.5).

strength_json_vehicle_count_type.description: What the numbers in strength_json.vehicles mean.

values.on_hand: Vehicles on hand, working order not stated.
values.unknown: The source does not say what the count means (for example vehicles committed in one action).

strength_json_scope.description: What part of the unit the figures in strength_json describe. Required whenever personnel is given (the validator reports an error if it is missing).

values.whole_unit: The figure covers the whole unit (division, brigade, ...) as the source states it.
values.sub_force: The figure covers only part of the unit: a battle group, a detachment or the force available for one task or line.
values.sector: The figure covers the forces in a sector or area that is not the unit's own organisation (for example the defenders of a line or beach, or all the forces landed on a beach).

boolean.description: Boolean fields (established, disestablished, destroyed) use lowercase text.

domain.description: Domain of a unit in data/units.csv (column domain; blank means ground).

values.ground: Ground forces (the default; blank means ground). Includes Luftwaffe ground formations such as parachute and field divisions, flak units, and coastal artillery whatever service owned it (Kriegsmarine coastal batteries; Scott, 4 and 13 November 2026, standing rule 23); `branch` records the service.
values.air: Air commands and flying units only (for example Fliegerkorps); not flak. Collected, not yet used in the main outputs.
values.naval: Naval commands and ships only; not coastal artillery. Collected, not yet used in the main outputs.

record_status.description: Research state of a unit record in data/units.csv.

values.placeholder: Identity only: the unit exists in the table so that other records can point to it. No claim file. Not a claim about its location.
values.partial: A claim file exists but coverage is known to be incomplete (for example only some operations are done).

source_token.description: Short tokens used in listing_source and initial_parent_source. See docs/sources.md and docs/methodology.md (Placeholder units).

values.LEX: Lexikon der Wehrmacht (lexikon-wehrmacht.de), the unit's own page or its timeline tables.
values.DEW6: de.wikipedia 'Schematische Kriegsgliederung der Wehrmacht fuer die Operation Overlord' (German order of battle for 6 June 1944).
values.WP12AG: en.wikipedia 'Twelfth United States Army Group' (order of battle, 8 May 1945).
values.WP6AG: en.wikipedia 'Sixth United States Army Group' (order of battle, 8 May 1945).
values.WPNORM: en.wikipedia 'List of Allied forces in the Normandy campaign'.
values.WPMG: en.wikipedia 'Operation Market Garden order of battle'.
values.WPBULGE: en.wikipedia 'Battle of the Bulge order of battle'.
values.WPUNIT: The unit's own en.wikipedia article (no Wikipedia order-of-battle page above links to it).

relationship_date_basis.description: Where the start and end dates of a command relation come from (columns date_basis, and stated_date_basis / stated_effective_to_basis on the claim link; valid_from_basis and valid_to_basis use these values and the extra ones of relation_start_basis and relation_end_basis).

values.order: A named order or message gives the date.
values.assignment_table: A dated assignment table such as CMH ETO-OB. The table date may differ from the day command actually passed.
values.narrative: A narrative history or reference work states the date.
values.inferred: The date is inferred from other rows; treat as approximate.

location_basis.description: How the claim's coordinate relates in time and place to the claim's date (optional claim column location_basis). Where a coordinate comes from a different date, record that date in location_date and the offset in location_temporal_offset_days.

values.documented_on_date: A source places the unit, event or headquarters at this location on the claim's date.
values.nearest_later_command_post: The coordinate is the nearest command post listed after the claim's date; the position on the date itself is not documented.
values.nearest_earlier_command_post: The coordinate is the nearest command post listed before the claim's date; the position on the date itself is not documented.
values.representative_point: A point chosen to stand for an area, front or named objective (not a documented position). Use it when location_represents is objective and the unit or headquarters was not at that place on the date.
values.town_centroid: The coordinate is the centre of a named town or commune; the source does not locate the headquarters or event more precisely.
values.operational_area: A point inside the area of operations (sector, landing area, bridgehead) rather than a headquarters or exact position.
values.inferred: Inferred from the unit's movements or other rows rather than stated.

op_type.description: Type of an operation row in data/operations.csv (column op_type).

values.umbrella: A planning or command umbrella that contains campaigns and operations (Overlord).
values.campaign: A campaign: a CMH campaign streamer (date_basis cmh_streamer) or a named campaign of the official histories (Brittany, Lorraine, Siegfried Line).
values.operation: A named operation with a codename or an official-history name (Cobra, Epsom, Market Garden, Lüttich).
values.battle: A battle or siege (Carentan, Cherbourg, Aachen, the Bulge, Bastogne).
values.phase: A phase of a larger operation without a name of its own (the pursuit, cutting the Cotentin).

operation_date_basis.description: Where the dates of an operation row come from (column date_basis).

values.cmh_streamer: Dates of a US Army campaign streamer (Center of Military History).
values.official_history: Dates from an official history: a US Army Green Book or CMH publication, or a national official history such as the Canadian Army official history (Stacey, The Victory Campaign).
values.secondary: Dates from Wikipedia or another secondary source.
values.derived: Dates set by the dataset authors from several sources, because no single source dates the phase; see notes.

operation_relation.description: Relation between two operations in data/operation_relations.csv (parent and child are given by parent_operation_id, not here).

values.follows: from_operation_id began after to_operation_id and continues or follows from it.
values.concurrent_with: The two ran at the same time in neighbouring areas without one being part of the other.
values.supports: from_operation_id was carried out in support of to_operation_id.
values.succeeded_by: from_operation_id was replaced by to_operation_id (a renamed, resumed or successor operation).
values.related: Linked in a way the other values do not capture, for example the German and Allied names of the same battle.

reference_role.description: Role of a claim-to-reference link in data/claim_reference_roles.csv: what in the claim the reference supports. A link with no row there has the role general.

values.event: The event definition: what happened (arrival, assignment, engagement, relief).
values.date: The date of the claim's event.
values.location: The place or the coordinates (a place source). The role of a gazetteer_geocoder reference (the coordinate service) is derived, not stored.
values.command_relationship: The unit's parent or attached/assigned relationship in command_relationships.
values.general: Supports the claim as a whole or the role is not established from the claim's own text (the default; no row is stored).

source_family.description: Source family of a reference (data/references_meta.csv source_family), used by the independent-source rubric: two references from the same family count once. The value is a free lower-case token (a host name with underscores) except for these families, which group sites that are not independent of each other.

values.wikipedia: Wikipedia in any language, its API and Wikimedia pages. One family however many articles are cited.
values.us_army_cmh: US Army Center of Military History publications and the sites that republish them (HyperWar copies of the Green Books, history.army.mil, archive copies of them).
values.openstreetmap: OpenStreetMap / Nominatim, the geocoder behind many coordinates. A gazetteer, not evidence that the unit was there.

alliance.description: Side of the war a nationality belongs to (column alliance of data/nationalities.csv).

values.nation: A single nation; the lowercase name is the folder under data/claims/.
values.multinational: A combined headquarters that belongs to no single nation (Allied).

echelon_rank.description: Rank of each organisational level for hierarchy checks (higher = larger formation) and the display order used in build/coverage.csv and docs/coverage.md. Read by scripts/validate.py, scripts/build.py, scripts/audit_temporal_relationships.py and scripts/who_controls.py through scripts/common.py; do not copy it into code. The rank 8 of `other` places higher or special headquarters above an army group; unlisted echelons rank 0 in the validator and 8 in the audits (unchanged behaviour). The naval ladder (naval_unit 10, naval_division 11, naval_squadron 12, task_group 13, fleet 14) has its own range so naval ranks never collide with ground ranks; the hierarchy check applies within the naval ladder only (scripts/validate.py check_command_relation_tables). display_order lists ground echelons only (the main outputs are ground).

echelon_id_letter.description: The echelon letter that ends a unit_id (`NATION-TYPE-NUMBER` + letter, see schema/README.md, "unit_id pattern"). An id that ends in a digit and one of these letters must have the matching echelon (checked by scripts/validate.py); an id that ends otherwise has no echelon letter. The echelons in `no_letter` never carry one: regiments, regiment-sized battle groups and battalions are identified by their type code and name or number (`GER-FJR-006`, `GER-KG-FREY`, `GER-SSHPZ-101`). Exception: the combat commands `US-CCA-002D` and `US-CCR-004D` (echelon `regiment/battle_group`), whose final `D` is the 2nd and 4th Armored Division in the id and not an echelon letter (`combat_command_pattern`). Ids are opaque and are never renamed to follow this rule. The naval-ladder echelons (naval_exempt) take no id letter, and a final letter on the id of such a unit is not an echelon letter (GER-MGW-000H, Marinegruppe West, is echelon fleet; ids are opaque and never renamed).

relationship_groups.description: Groups of command-relationship values used by the checks and the derived tables (single source for scripts/validate.py, scripts/audit_temporal_relationships.py and scripts/who_controls.py).

higher_than_organic.description: For each echelon, the higher echelons whose headquarters cannot be an `organic` parent (a division, corps or army under a higher headquarters is assigned, attached, unspecified_subordination or operational_control). scripts/validate.py warns when `organic` is used across these pairs.

source_type.description: Kind of source of a row in data/references_meta.csv (column source_type).

values.official_history: A government or armed-forces official history (for example a US Army Green Book volume).
values.unit_history: A history written by or about the unit.
values.assignment_table: A table of unit assignments (for example an order of battle by date).
values.reference_compilation: A reference compilation such as a unit or order-of-battle web reference.
values.gazetteer_geocoder: A gazetteer or geocoding service used for coordinates only.
values.monument_or_memorial: A monument, memorial or memorial-site page.
values.archive_document: An archived primary or period document.
values.news_or_web_article: A news report or other web article.

relation_start_basis.description: Where valid_from of a command relation comes from: a sourced date (the values of relationship_date_basis), or claim_date when no source dates the start and valid_from is the date of the first claim that lists the relation.

values.order: A named order or message gives the date.
values.assignment_table: A dated assignment table such as CMH ETO-OB. The table date may differ from the day command actually passed.
values.narrative: A narrative history or reference work states the date.
values.inferred: The date is inferred from other rows; treat as approximate.
values.claim_date: No source dates the start: valid_from is the date of the first claim that lists the relation (the relation may have begun earlier).

relation_end_basis.description: Where valid_to of a command relation comes from: a sourced date (the values of relationship_date_basis), or one of the two derived cases below. A missing sourced end never means indefinitely valid.

values.order: A named order or message gives the date.
values.assignment_table: A dated assignment table such as CMH ETO-OB. The table date may differ from the day command actually passed.
values.narrative: A narrative history or reference work states the date.
values.inferred: The date is inferred from other rows; treat as approximate.
values.inferred_from_next_claim: No source dates the end: valid_to is the day before the unit's next claim that no longer lists the relation; valid_to_earliest is the last claim date that lists it, so the true end lies between the two.
values.open_at_last_claim: No end is recorded: the unit's latest claim still lists the relation, valid_to is blank.

relation_claim_role.description: What a claim says about a command relation (column role of data/command_relation_claims.csv). For a claim of the subject unit the role follows from which dates the claim itself stated; a claim of the higher unit that lists the subject has the role listed_by_higher_unit.

values.asserts_start: The claim states when the relation began (stated_effective_from).
values.asserts_end: The claim states when the relation ended (stated_effective_to).
values.asserts_start_and_end: The claim states both the start and the end.
values.observed_during: The claim lists the relation as in force on its date without dating the start or the end.
values.listed_by_higher_unit: The claim belongs to the HIGHER unit of the relation and lists the subject as one of its components with this relationship (for example a corps claim whose composing_units names a division attached to it, or a division claim that names an attached battle group). It is evidence for the relation, not one of the claim's own relationships: it does not appear in the claim's rebuilt command_relationships, it needs no stated dates (it records what the claim said in stated_note, and the start or end only if the claim gave one), and the subject must be listed in the claim's composing_units (or, until converted, named by id in composing_text).

relation_overlap_kind.description: Why two contradictory command relations overlap (column kind of data/command_relation_overlaps.csv). Every such overlap must be listed; the validator rejects an unlisted or stale one.

values.transfer_dates_differ: The two relations are consecutive (the unit moved from one higher unit of an echelon to another) but the sources date the change differently, or one end is only inferred, so the intervals overlap on some days. Nothing is resolved.
values.concurrent_by_source: A source states that the unit was under both higher units at the same time.

place_kind.description: What a place in data/places.csv is. One point stands for it in every case.

values.point: A named settlement or site: a town, village, hamlet, château, hill or station.
values.area: A named area, sector, beach, zone, bridgehead or other stretch of ground, represented by one point (usually the centre of the town or place it is geocoded to).
values.line: A front, defensive line, axis of advance or route, represented by one point on it.
values.sea_position: A point at sea: a ship or submarine position given by a source, or worked from an anchor place, a distance and a bearing (say how in coord_source_note). Claims at a sea_position place are capped at confidence 0.5 (scripts/validate.py). The country is the nearest coast. Added in the air-naval schema pass, 13 November 2026.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes used by places.country (the country the point lies in today). Add a code with its name when a place in a new country is added.

strength_json_status.description: The `status` key of strength_json: the qualitative strength a source states for the unit on that date. `destroyed` is not allowed here: it is derived from the claim's destroyed flag. No status means strength_status unknown.

values.full: A source describes the unit as at full strength.
values.reduced: Source states significant losses or reduced combat power.
values.heavily_depleted: Source states the unit was a small fraction of its strength.

activity_status.description: Optional claim column activity_status: the unit's state of availability, not its action on the day (that is event_type and current_activity). Five values, chosen to be decidable from the official histories; see docs/activity_status_design.md.

values.in_line: Holding or fighting on a sector of the front (including a quiet sector).
values.reserve: Out of the line but available for commitment: corps, army or army-group reserve, or held back behind the front.
values.refitting: Withdrawn to rest, receive replacements and re-equip; not available for commitment until the refit ends. Includes the German "rehabilitation" (Auffrischung).
values.garrison: Holding a fixed place (fortress, port, occupied town) with no field role.
values.transit: Moving between theatres or regions by road, rail or sea, and not available on the way.

activity_basis.description: How the activity_status of a row is known.

values.stated: A source cited on the row says it in words (for example "resting and refitting", "in corps reserve").
values.inferred: Deduced from the row or from neighbouring rows; the reading carries a confidence of at most 0.3 whatever the row confidence.

activity_span.description: The part of an activity span that a row records.

values.start: The activity begins on the row date.
values.end: The activity of the same value, opened by an earlier start row of the unit, ends on the row date.
values.point: The activity is observed on the row date only; it opens no span.

lineage_kind.description: Meaning of the kind column of data/unit_lineage.csv: how a successor unit record continues a predecessor record. Each unit record stays separate; a lineage row only links them.

values.redesignation: The same formation takes a new designation; personnel and organisation continue (for example the 462nd Infantry Division becoming the 462nd Volksgrenadier Division).
values.reconstitution_from_remnants: The predecessor was destroyed or broken up and the successor was formed with its remnants (usually together with a new or forming formation), as the source states.
values.absorbed_into: The predecessor (for example a division still forming) was merged into or renamed as the successor and ceased to exist on its own.
values.formed_from_remnants: A different kind of formation was formed from the remnants of the predecessor (for example a panzer brigade formed from the remnants of a panzergrenadier division).

scope.description: Scope marker of a unit in data/units.csv (column scope; blank means in_scope). Standing rule 22 (Scott, 13 November 2026): a claim is recorded even when its unit is outside the current scope (any domain, front or period). Out-of-scope units, their claims and their command relations stay out of the main outputs and the who_controls grid and are written to build/other_domains/.

values.in_scope: The unit is inside the current scope (the default; blank means in_scope). Ground units in scope feed the main outputs.
values.out_of_scope: The unit is outside the current scope (another front or period, another domain). Collected for later; its coverage and balance figures are incidental, not surveyed.

ship_type.description: Ship type of a unit with echelon naval_unit (column ship_type of data/units.csv and of data/ship_classes.csv): US hull classification codes with plain-English labels. National terms (Torpedoboot, escort destroyer, Panzerschiff) stay in the unit or class note. Added in the air-naval schema pass, 13 November 2026; docs/air_naval_pilot.md section 6.3.

values.CA: heavy cruiser (also the German Panzerschiff, noted)
values.DE: destroyer escort (also the Royal Navy escort destroyer, for example the Hunt class)
values.PG: gunboat or sloop (Royal Navy sloops, patrol gunboats)
values.SS: submarine (any navy; midget submarines too, noted)

ship_capability_key.description: Keys of the capabilities_json object of data/ship_classes.csv and of the capabilities object inside strength_json of a naval claim (a refit). Each key holds {value, unit, reference_id, note}; a key is absent when no source gives it.

values.standard_displacement: Standard (or design) displacement as the source states it.
